Exception type thrown by gsl::narrow when a narrowing conversion changes the value. It derives from std::exception and overrides what() to return the literal "narrowing_error". No additional state is stored.

An 8-bit byte type for GSL. When the standard library's std::byte is available and enabled (GSL_USE_STD_BYTE == 1), gsl::byte is a deprecated alias of std::byte and gsl::impl::byte is also an alias to std::byte. Otherwise, it defines an enum class byte : unsigned char with bitwise and shift operators and a to_integer helper. Use it to represent raw byte data without implicit arithmetic conversions.

Only applicable when GSL_USE_STD_BYTE == 1. In that configuration, gsl::byte and gsl::impl::byte are aliases of std::byte from <cstddef>. The canonical type is std::byte, which is a scoped enumeration representing a byte-sized unit of storage. This entry documents that the effective underlying type is std::byte; construction is via standard facilities. No definition is present in this header.

functions.name: std::copy
functions.signature:
template <class InputIt, class OutputIt>
OutputIt copy(InputIt first, InputIt last, OutputIt d_first);
functions.description: Copies the elements in the range [first, last) to a destination range beginning at d_first, preserving order. Commonly used to move data between containers/arrays or into an output iterator. Returns an iterator to the end of the destination range after the last copied element.
requirements: InputIt must meet the requirements of at least an input iterator; OutputIt must meet the requirements of at least an output iterator for the value type of InputIt.
The source range [first, last) must be valid: first and last must be reachable, and each iterator in the range must be dereferenceable.
The destination range beginning at d_first must be valid for at least std::distance(first, last) assignments.
The source and destination ranges must not overlap; overlapping ranges result in undefined behavior (use std::copy_backward for overlapping ranges).
Copying may propagate exceptions thrown by element copy/assignment operations; callers should be prepared to handle such exceptions.

functions.name: gsl::narrow_cast

constexpr T narrow_cast(U u) noexcept;
functions.description: Performs an unchecked, explicit narrowing conversion of u to type T, equivalent to static_cast<T>(u). Intended for documenting intent where narrowing is acceptable and no runtime checking is desired. Use when you know the value fits the target type.
requirements: T must be explicitly convertible from U (the conversion must be well-formed).
The caller accepts potential loss of information; no runtime checks are performed.
Evaluated in a constant expression context if possible; function is noexcept and will not throw.

functions.name: gsl::finally
functions.signature:
template <class F>
auto finally(F&& f) noexcept(/* dependent on F */);
functions.description: Creates a scope guard that invokes the provided callable f exactly once when the guard object is destroyed (typically at scope exit). Useful for RAII-style cleanup actions such as unlocking, closing, or reverting state. Returns a small guard object that holds f.
requirements: F must be callable with no arguments and no required return value (invoked as f()).
Do not allow the callable to throw when invoked from the guard's destructor; throwing during stack unwinding will call std::terminate.

The returned guard must have automatic storage duration or otherwise be destroyed at the desired cleanup point; if it is released early (e.g., moved and then destroyed elsewhere), cleanup timing follows that object’s lifetime.
F should be move-constructible; exact noexcept specification depends on whether F is nothrow-move-constructible.

functions.name: gsl::narrow
functions.signature:
template <class T, class U>
T narrow(U u);
functions.description: Performs a checked narrowing conversion of u to type T. If the value cannot be represented exactly (or, for integers, if the value would change after converting to T and back), it signals failure by throwing an exception (typically gsl::narrowing_error). Use when you want runtime enforcement against lossy conversions.
requirements: T must be explicitly convertible from U (the conversion must be well-formed).

If the converted value cannot be represented in T without loss of information, the function throws (e.g., gsl::narrowing_error). Callers should be prepared to handle this exception or ensure the input fits.
Availability depends on exception support: the narrow() header is only included when __cpp_exceptions is defined in this translation unit, per the provided header.

functions.name: gsl::narrow

constexpr T gsl::narrow(U u)
functions.description: Checked narrowing conversion from U to T for arithmetic destination types. Converts u to T using narrow_cast (i.e., static_cast), then verifies that converting back to U preserves the original value and that a signed/unsigned mismatch does not change sign. Throws gsl::narrowing_error if the value changes or if a sign change would occur. Note: NaN will always trigger an exception because NaN != NaN. Typical usage is to safely convert between arithmetic types while detecting lossy or sign-changing conversions.
requirements: T must satisfy std::is_arithmetic<T>::value.
U must be convertible to T via static_cast (as used by narrow_cast<T>(u)).
T must be convertible back to U via static_cast<U>(t).
Equality comparison for U must be valid (uses operator==/!= between U values).
Less-than comparison with zero must be valid for both T and U (uses t < T{} and u < U{}).
Callers must handle potential exceptions: throws gsl::narrowing_error when the conversion changes the value or sign.
Inputs that are NaN will cause an exception due to NaN != NaN.

Typical usage is to perform value-preserving casts to non-arithmetic types where round-tripping via U must not change the value. Details of T are unknown beyond being non-arithmetic; behavior depends on T and U supporting the required casts and comparisons.
requirements: T must satisfy !std::is_arithmetic<T>::value.
U must be convertible to T via static_cast (as used by narrow_cast<T>(u)).
T must be convertible back to U via static_cast<U>(t).
Equality comparison for U must be valid (uses operator==/!= between U values).
Callers must handle potential exceptions: throws gsl::narrowing_error when the conversion changes the value.

functions.name: gsl::copy
functions.signature:
template <class SrcElementType, std::size_t SrcExtent, class DestElementType, std::size_t DestExtent>
void gsl::copy(gsl::span<SrcElementType, SrcExtent> src, gsl::span<DestElementType, DestExtent> dest)
functions.description: Copies elements from the source span to the destination span using std::copy_n. Intended as a fast span-to-span copy. Use when you have two gsl::span ranges and want to assign each element from src to the corresponding element in dest in order. Performs element-wise assignment; order is preserved.
requirements: Precondition: dest.size() >= src.size() (enforced at runtime via Expects).
Compile-time: If both spans have static extents, SrcExtent <= DestExtent (enforced via static_assert).
Compile-time: The destination element type must be assignable from the source element type (std::is_assignable<decltype(*dest.data()), decltype(*src.data())>).
The source and destination ranges must not overlap (requirement of std::copy_n).
Both src and dest must be valid gsl::span objects referring to contiguous memory with at least size() elements available.

functions.name: gsl::final_action::final_action
functions.signature:
template <class F>
gsl::final_action<F>::final_action(const F& ff) noexcept
functions.description: Constructs a final_action that stores a copy of the callable ff and will invoke it once when the final_action object is destroyed (scope exit), unless it has been moved-from. Use to ensure cleanup code runs on scope exit (RAII).
requirements: F must be a callable type invocable with no arguments (i.e., an expression f() must be well-formed).
The stored callable must not throw on invocation, because the destructor is noexcept and any exception will call std::terminate.
Construction is noexcept; callers should not rely on exceptions from construction.

gsl::final_action<F>::final_action(F&& ff) noexcept
functions.description: Move-constructs the stored callable from ff and creates a final_action that will invoke it on destruction (scope exit), unless moved-from later. Prefer this overload when passing temporaries or movable callables.
requirements: F must be a callable type invocable with no arguments (i.e., an expression f() must be well-formed).
The stored callable must not throw on invocation, because the destructor is noexcept and any exception will call std::terminate.

functions.name: gsl::final_action::~final_action
functions.signature:
template <class F>
gsl::final_action<F>::~final_action() noexcept
functions.description: Destructor. If this object still owns the action (i.e., has not been moved-from), invokes the stored callable. Intended to run cleanup code at scope exit.
requirements: The stored callable must be safe to call at the time of destruction.
The callable must not throw; throwing from this noexcept destructor will call std::terminate.
May be invoked during stack unwinding; ensure the callable is safe in that context.

functions.name: gsl::finally

template <class F>
GSL_NODISCARD auto gsl::finally(F&& f) noexcept -> gsl::final_action<std::decay_t<F>>
functions.description: Factory function that creates a final_action from a callable f. Use as: auto guard = gsl::finally([&]{ cleanup(); }); The returned guard will invoke f when it goes out of scope.
requirements: F must be a callable invocable with no arguments.
The callable must not throw when invoked, since final_action's destructor is noexcept.
Callers should keep the returned object alive until the desired scope exit; discarding it immediately negates any effect.
Function is noexcept and will not throw during guard creation.

functions.name: gsl::operator<<=
functions.signature:
template <class IntegerType, std::enable_if_t<std::is_integral<IntegerType>::value, bool> = true>
constexpr gsl::byte& gsl::operator<<=(gsl::byte& b, IntegerType shift) noexcept
functions.description: Left-shift-assign a gsl::byte by an integral shift amount. Modifies b by shifting its underlying 8-bit value left by shift and returns b. Only provided when GSL provides its own gsl::byte (i.e., when GSL_USE_STD_BYTE == 0).
requirements: IntegerType must be an integral type (enforced via SFINAE).
b must be a valid, initialized gsl::byte lvalue.
Shift count must be in the range [0, 7]; shifting by a count >= 8 is undefined behavior for an 8-bit value.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: gsl::details::default_terminate_handler
functions.signature: [[noreturn]] inline void __cdecl gsl::details::default_terminate_handler()
functions.description: Default termination handler used on MSVC when the no-exceptions workaround is enabled. It forcibly terminates the process via __fastfail(RANGE_CHECKS_FAILURE). Intended to be installed as the terminate handler used by gsl::details::terminate() under that configuration.
requirements: Availability: This function is only defined when GSL_MSVC_USE_STL_NOEXCEPTION_WORKAROUND is enabled (MSVC, kernel/no-exception modes).
Behavior: Never returns; it unconditionally terminates the process.
Usage: Typically invoked indirectly via gsl::details::terminate() or by setting it as the current terminate handler.

functions.name: gsl::details::get_terminate_handler
functions.signature: inline gsl::details::terminate_handler& gsl::details::get_terminate_handler() noexcept
functions.description: Returns a reference to the internal process-wide terminate handler pointer used by gsl::details::terminate() on MSVC when the no-exceptions workaround is enabled. Callers can read or assign this to customize termination behavior.
requirements: Availability: This accessor is only defined when GSL_MSVC_USE_STL_NOEXCEPTION_WORKAROUND is enabled (MSVC, kernel/no-exception modes).
Return: Provides a reference to a static gsl::details::terminate_handler (typedef void(__cdecl*)()).
Assignment: If assigning, the target must be a valid function pointer of type void(__cdecl*)() that does not return (to preserve the [[noreturn]] contract of gsl::details::terminate()).
Lifetime: Any installed handler must remain valid for the duration of the program.
Exception-safety: noexcept; callers must not throw exceptions from within the handler in no-exception configurations.

functions.name: gsl::details::terminate
functions.signature: [[noreturn]] inline void gsl::details::terminate() noexcept
functions.description: Terminates the program. On MSVC with the no-exceptions workaround, it invokes the currently installed terminate handler (defaulting to gsl::details::default_terminate_handler). Otherwise it delegates to std::terminate(). Used by GSL contract checks (e.g., Expects/Ensures) to abort on violation.
requirements: Behavior: Never returns; callers must not rely on execution continuing after the call.
Availability: Always defined; behavior depends on build configuration.

Handler usage (MSVC no-exception mode): If a custom handler is installed via get_terminate_handler(), it must conform to type void(__cdecl*)() and should not return to maintain the [[noreturn]] guarantee.
Noexcept: Must not throw; any attempt to throw would result in termination by the runtime.
